thread.title_full: Floyd County schools top state CCRPI average; Rome sees growth - NewsBreak

author: rhartdegen
title: Floyd County schools top state CCRPI average; Rome sees growth - NewsBreak
text:
By rhartdegen ,
5 hours ago Floyd County Schools Rome City Schools Logos The scores are in. Floyd County Schools consistently exceeded state averages and Rome City Schools saw improvement in scores, according to the state’s 2025 College and Career Ready Performance Index.
The CCRPI, released last week, measures students’ performance in five categories: Content Mastery, Progress, Closing Gaps, Readiness and, for high schools, Graduation Rate.
The Georgia Department of Education calculates scores using data from the previous school year and provides composite scores for each category for elementary, middle and high schools.
The Content Mastery score rates students’ preparedness for the next grade, college or career by calculating their mastery in English, math and science.
Readiness measures how prepared they are for the next level using factors such as literacy, attendance and participation in extracurricular activities.
Progress rates growth in each of those topics and Closing Gaps is a measure of how students are achieving set academic goals.
Floyd County and Rome City schools officials expressed pride in their scores, but each school system used different categories to measure success. FCS focused on content mastery, while RCS focused on progress.
Floyd County Schools
The county schools scored higher than the state average across the board in content mastery and readiness, according to the CCRPI.
The county schools saw the most significant difference in scores compared to the state in content mastery. As a whole, the elementary schools scored 10.5 points above the state average, middle schools scored 7.4 points above and high schools scored 13.3 points above.
FCS scored below the state average at the elementary and middle school levels in the closing gaps category. The county schools also scored below the state average in progress at the elementary level.
“These results are a testament to the dedication of our educators and the hard work of our students,” said Assistant Superintendent and Chief Academic Officer John Parker. “We are incredibly proud of everyone involved. As a school system and a community, we remain committed to delivering a high-quality education that equips our students for college and career success.”
Floyd County Schools also surpassed the state’s graduation rate by 9.1 points, with a 96.3% graduation rate.
Rome City Schools
Rome City Schools exceeded the state average at the elementary level in progress and closing gaps, and at the high school level in readiness, but scored below the state average in the remaining nine areas.
However, the 2025 scores tell a story of growth for RCS, especially in the elementary schools, which improved across all four categories.
In the progress category, elementary schools reported a 10.2-point increase, and middle schools reported a 5-point increase, compared to last year. The city schools also reported growth in content mastery for elementary and high schools, and in readiness for elementary and middle schools.
“Rome City Schools continues to see steady growth as we strengthen our academic foundation,” said Superintendent Eric L. Holland. “With the continued support from our school board and a laser-sharp focus on student engagement and teacher empowerment, we have been successful at elevating student learning across all grade levels.
The Rome City Schools’ graduation rate also exceeded the state average by 8.5 points, at 95.7%.
